subject: MAP Sponsor Orientation & Escalation Ladder — Aurora Health
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Burke <alex.burke@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-12-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: MAP Sponsor Orientation & Escalation Ladder — Aurora Health

Hi Alex — great to meet earlier. Per our conversation I wanted to: 1) introduce the Redwood sponsor team, 2) share a first-draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP), and 3) outline an escalation ladder so your execs have clear points of contact.

Sponsor team (Redwood):
- Rachel Kim — Account Executive (primary contact for commercial & scheduling)
- Marcus Lin — VP, Solutions (exec sponsor / product alignment)
- Karthik Iyer — Solutions Architect (technical lead for evals)

Proposed MAP milestones (first pass):
- 12/10: Delivery of evaluation environment + onboarding guide
- 12/20: Performance & latency evaluation (sample workloads)
- 12/22: Security questionnaire follow-up and evidence exchange
- 01/05: Procurement & PO submission target
- 01/15: Pilot acceptance / go/no-go decision

Attached: Aurora_MAP_Draft_2026-12-01.xlsx (draft MAP) and our completed security questionnaire (security_questionnaire_filled.pdf).

Ask: Could you confirm the Aurora exec sponsor for this MAP (VP/CTO level) and name the internal escalation contact we should route to if any blocker reaches exec level? Also please confirm whether the proposed milestone dates look reasonable.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning timelines so we can get the evaluation started before year-end.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
(rachel.kim@redwood.ai)
(attachment: Aurora_MAP_Draft_2026-12-01.xlsx)
(attachment: security_questionnaire_filled.pdf)

From: Alex Burke <alex.burke@aurorahealth.com>

Subject: Re: MAP Sponsor Orientation & Escalation Ladder — Aurora Health

Rachel — thanks for the clear summary. Quick responses:
- I'll serve as the exec sponsor for the MAP (VP of Engineering).
- Please loop Maya Patil (Head of Security) for the security threads — she will own evidence review and the compliance gate.
- Procurement contact for PO & contracting will be Susan Leong.

The timeline is mostly fine, though our security team prefers a little more lead time for evidence review. Can we move the security follow-up to 12/24 and target performance validation the week of 12/27? We have some freeze windows during the holidays but can make exceptions for a short, timeboxed eval.

Also CC'ing Susan and Maya — Susan, can you confirm procurement timelines on your side?

—Alex
Alex Burke
VP, Engineering | Aurora Health
(alex.burke@aurorahealth.com)

Thanks all — Rachel

Heads-up on the evaluation plan from engineering side:
- We'll provision a dedicated evaluation instance with the following profile: 8x A100 (for throughput testing) and a 2x A10 config for lower-cost latency runs.
- Expected sample workload: 1000 concurrent short-sessions (avg seq len 128) and a separate batch for 200 long-session samples (avg seq len 1024).
- K/V cache warmup: recommend a 30-minute warmup with representative prefixes to avoid cold-start skew.

For security/integration: we can provide scoped logs and tracing hooks to your security team (Maya) and enable audit log exports to your S3 bucket; we will also share a short runbook so your engineers can replay the eval if needed.

I attached a short tech checklist to the MAP (see attachment) and flagged items that may affect the 12/28 performance window (network egress limits, test dataset anonymization).
